findings.suggested_fix: Adapt the existing started-generation drain pattern to rewrite jobs: commit a durable in-flight marker under short owner/consent/parent locks, perform the provider await outside those locks, then reacquire and revalidate authority and lease for atomic projection/finalization. Withdrawal and erasure must cancel unsent work and drain admitted sends before acknowledging, including crash/expired-lease handling. Preserve the current credential revocation barrier; do not simply remove owned_credential locking. Add an isolated PostgreSQL fake-provider regression showing /session and private-page reads complete while generation is paused, alongside the existing revoke/erase/fence regressions.
findings.title: Background rewrites block foreground session checks
findings.why_it_matters: With the optional rewrite pilot enabled, navigating to a private page or returning to its tab can stall behind that owner's background provider request, even with only one beta user. Credential lookup now always takes the guest row's FOR UPDATE lock, while execution_guard holds that same row through the provider await; an allowed call lasting more than 15 seconds exceeds the browser request timeout and SessionBoundary then hides the page with an offline warning despite a working connection. Waiting for an admitted send during erasure or withdrawal is intentional, but making ordinary session checks wait for it undermines the deterministic-content fallback. Separating the durable send/drain fence from foreground credential authorization removes this dependency without dropping the revocation and erasure guarantees.
findings.validation_reason: Inspected current WIP still holds the same owner FOR UPDATE lock through provider I/O and foreground /session authorization. An enabled, admitted rewrite with more than 15 seconds of remaining provider wait can time out the browser and show an offline page. Production incidence and end-to-end latency were not measured; disabled flags prevent activation, not the defect.
